arxiv-2012-15699.title: Better Robustness by More Coverage: Adversarial and Mixup Data Augmentation for Robust Finetuning
arxiv-2012-15699.creator: Chenglei Si, Zhengyan Zhang, Fanchao Qi, Zhiyuan Liu, Yasheng Wang, Qun Liu, Maosong Sun
arxiv-2012-15699.description: Abstract Pretrained language models (PLMs) perform poorly under adversarial attacks. To improve the adversarial robustness, adversarial data augmentation (ADA) has been widely adopted to cover more search space of adversarial attacks by adding textual adversarial examples during training. However, the number of adversarial examples for text augmentation is still extremely insufficient due to the exponentially large attack search space.

arxiv-2104-14119.title: Adaptive Partitioning Strategy for High-Dimensional Discrete Simulation-based Optimization Problems
arxiv-2104-14119.creator: Jing Lu, Tianli Zhou, Carolina Osorio
arxiv-2104-14119.description: Abstract Abstract In this paper, we introduce a technique to enhance the computational efficiency of solution algorithms for high-dimensional discrete simulation-based optimization problems. The technique is based on innovative adaptive partitioning strategies that partition the feasible region using solutions that has already been simulated as well as prior knowledge of the problem of interesting.

arxiv-2111-00750.title: Appearance of Keplerian discs orbiting on both sides of a reflection-symmetric wormhole
arxiv-2111-00750.creator: Jan Schee, Zdeněk Stuchlík
arxiv-2111-00750.description: Abstract We construct optical appearance and profiled spectral lines of Keplerian discs with inner edge at the innermost circular geodesic located on both sides of the reflection-symmetric Simpson-Visser wormhole, in dependence on its parameter and inclination angle of a distant observer.

arxiv-2201-05836.title: Temporal quality of post-compressed pulses at large compression factors
arxiv-2201-05836.creator: Esmerando Escoto, Anne-Lise Viotti, Skirmantas Alisauskas, Henrik Tünnermann, Ingmar Hartl, Christoph M. Heyl
arxiv-2201-05836.description: Abstract Post-compression of ultra-short laser pulses via self-phase modulation is routinely employed for the generation of laser pulses with optical bandwidths reaching far beyond the laser gain limitations. While high compression factors can be routinely achieved, the compressed pulses typically suffer from temporal quality degradation.

arxiv-2302-13730.title: Multi-configurational nature of electron correlation within nitrogen vacancy centers in diamond
arxiv-2302-13730.creator: Yilin Chen, Tonghuan Jiang, Haoxiang Chen, Erxun Han, Ali Alavi, Kuang Yu, Enge Wang, Ji Chen
arxiv-2302-13730.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yilin Chen, Tonghuan Jiang, Haoxiang Chen, Erxun Han, Ali Alavi, Kuang Yu, Enge Wang, Ji Chen. Diamond is a solid-state platform to develop quantum technologies, but it has been a long-standing problem that the current understanding of quantum states in diamond is mostly limited to single-electron pictures. Here, we combine the full configuration interaction quantum Monte Carlo method and the density-matrix functional embedding theory, to achieve unprecedented accuracy in describing the many-body quantum states of nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers in diamond.

arxiv-2303-02647.title: Fast Discrete Fourier Transform algorithms requiring less than 0( N ​ log ⁡ N N\log N ) multiplications
arxiv-2303-02647.creator: Ryszard M. Stasiński
arxiv-2303-02647.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ryszard M. Stasiński. In the paper it is shown that there exist infinite classes of fast DFT algorithms having multiplicative complexity lower than O ⁡ ( N ​ log ⁡ N ) O(N\log N) , i.e. smaller than their arithmetical complexity.

arxiv-2304-13905.title: LSTM based IoT Device Identification
arxiv-2304-13905.creator: Kahraman Kostas
arxiv-2304-13905.description: Abstract While the use of the Internet of Things is becoming more and more popular, many security vulnerabilities are emerging with the large number of devices being introduced to the market. In this environment, IoT device identification methods provide a preventive security measure as an important factor in identifying these devices and detecting the vulnerabilities they suffer from.

arxiv-2311-09896.title: Thermalization rate of polaritons in strongly-coupled molecular systems
arxiv-2311-09896.creator: Evgeny A. Tereshchenkov, Ivan V. Panyukov, Mikhail Misko, Vladislav Yu. Shishkov, Evgeny S. Andrianov, Anton V. Zasedatelev
arxiv-2311-09896.description: Abstract Polariton thermalization is a key process in achieving light-matter Bose–Einstein condensation, spanning from solid-state semiconductor microcavities at cryogenic temperatures to surface plasmon nanocavities with molecules at room temperature. Originated from the matter component of polariton states, the microscopic mechanisms of thermalization are closely tied to specific material properties. In this work, we investigate polariton thermalization in strongly-coupled molecular systems.

arxiv-2404-13458.title: Generalization of Task Parameterized Dynamical Systems using Gaussian Process Transportation
arxiv-2404-13458.creator: Giovanni Franzese, Ravi Prakash, Jens Kober
arxiv-2404-13458.description: Abstract Learning from Interactive Demonstrations has revolutionized the way non-expert humans teach robots. It is enough to kinesthetically move the robot around to teach pick-and-place, dressing, or cleaning policies. However, the main challenge is correctly generalizing to novel situations, e.g., different surfaces to clean or different arm postures to dress.

arxiv-2505-18617.title: Tuning the flexural frequency of overhang-/T-shaped microcantilevers for high harmonics
arxiv-2505-18617.creator: Le Tri Dat, Chi Cuong Nguyen, Nguyen Duy Vy, Amir F. Payam
arxiv-2505-18617.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Le Tri Dat, Chi Cuong Nguyen, Nguyen Duy Vy, Amir F. Payam. High-harmonic (HH) frequencies in microcantilever impose several applications in precision detection thanks to the higher sensitivity of the higher modes in comparison to the fundamental modes. In this study, we showed that by tuning the cantilever length via changing the clamped position, the dimensional ratio of the overhang to the main cantilever part is altered and the HHs could be effectively obtained.

arxiv-2508-09207.title: GANime: Generating Anime and Manga Character Drawings from Sketches with Deep Learning
arxiv-2508-09207.creator: Tai Vu, Robert Yang
arxiv-2508-09207.description: Abstract The process of generating fully colorized drawings from sketches is a large, usually costly bottleneck in the manga and anime industry. In this study, we examine multiple models for image-to-image translation between anime characters and their sketches, including Neural Style Transfer, C-GAN, and CycleGAN.

pmc-10669509.title: The Juvenile-Hormone-Responsive Factor AmKr-h1 Regulates Caste Differentiation in Honey Bees
pmc-10669509.creator: Zhi-Xian Gong, Fu-Ping Cheng, Jia-Ning Xu, Wei-Yu Yan, Zi-Long Wang, Mauro Mandrioli
pmc-10669509.description: Honey bees are typical model organisms for the study of caste differentiation, and the juvenile hormone (JH) is a crucial link in the regulatory network of caste differentiation in honey bees. To investigate the mechanism of JH-mediated caste differentiation, we analyzed the effect of the JH response gene AmKr-h1 on this process.

pmc-11357919.title: Multi-omics characterization of type 2 diabetes mellitus-induced gastroenteropathy in the db/db mouse model
pmc-11357919.creator: Yuxin Zhang, Yanjiao Zhang, Ruiyang Yin, Xinyi Fang, Runyu Miao, Huifang Guan, Yiqi Yao, Jiaxing Tian
pmc-11357919.description: ObjectiveGastrointestinal dysfunction are often associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), a complicated metabolic illness. Contributing factors have been proposed, including genetic predisposition, gene environmental, and lifestyle interactions, but the pathophysiology remains unknown.MethodsWe aim to explore the possible causes behind gastrointestinal dysfunction caused by type 2 diabetes in this study.

pmc-11461959.title: Moyamoya syndrome secondary to MELAS syndrome in a child: A case report and literature revue
pmc-11461959.creator: Fatima Zohra Benbrahim, Siham El Haddad, Nazik Allali, Latifa Chat
pmc-11461959.description: Mitochondrial myopathy with lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes is a rare mitochondrial disorder, most often revealed by symptoms and signs that typically include mitochondrial myopathy, encephalopathy with stroke-like episodes, seizures and/or dementia, and lactic acidosis. Imaging findings, although diverse, usually present characteristic features that help differentiate these disorders from vascular syndromes.

pmc-11582429.title: Design and fabrication of self-calibration colorimetric/fluorescence/SERS tri-modal optical sensor for highly rapid and accurate detection of mercury ions in foods
pmc-11582429.creator: Jinxin Chen, Cheng Zhang, Lunzhao Yi, Fengmin Duan, Ying Gu, Kun Ge, Xuejing Fan
pmc-11582429.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The improvement of detection accuracy without loss of rapidity and sensitivity by optical sensors in complex food analysis is still full of challenges owing to the matrix interference. Herein, a novel and simple self-calibration colorimetric/fluorescence/surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) tri-modal optical sensor based on aminated Rhodamine 6G (R6G-NH2) was developed for highly rapid, sensitive, and accurate detection of Hg2+ in food samples.

pmc-12371040.title: Mirabegron nighttime versus daytime dosing for women with overactive bladder syndrome: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-12371040.creator: Sheng-Mou Hsiao
pmc-12371040.description: The effect of nighttime dosing versus daytime dosing of mirabegron is undetermined. Thus, this study aimed to clarify the effect of nighttime versus daytime mirabegron dosing. Between August 2017 and August 2023, all women with overactive bladder syndrome were randomly assigned to receive mirabegron 25 mg once with nighttime or daytime dosing for 12 weeks.

pmc-12417328.title: Successful Management of Cerebral Salt‐Wasting Syndrome in a Child With Epileptic Encephalopathy: A Case Report
pmc-12417328.creator: Rui Zhang, Yi Deng, Wenjing Li
pmc-12417328.description: This case highlights the integral role of clinical pharmacists in the treatment process and suggests that fludrocortisone can serve as a safe and effective treatment option for CSWS in pediatric patients, especially when standard sodium supplementation and rehydration are insufficient.

pmc-12450282.title: Sveinsson Chorioretinal Atrophy: A New Gene Variant
pmc-12450282.creator: Ricardo A Murati Calderon, Sebastián J Vázquez-Folch, Natalio Izquierdo
pmc-12450282.description: We report the case of a 61-year-old Hispanic female patient with clinical features consistent with Sveinsson chorioretinal atrophy (SCRA), including bilateral peripapillary chorioretinal atrophy and early macular involvement. The patient presented with no significant visual complaints but demonstrated reduced visual acuity in the left eye and characteristic peripheral fundus findings.

pmc-12452330.title: Impact of a 24-Week Workplace Physical Activity Program on Oxidative Stress Markers, Metabolic Health, and Physical Fitness: A Pilot Study in a Real-World Academic Setting
pmc-12452330.creator: Gabriele Maisto, Maria Scatigna, Simona Delle Monache, Maria Francesca Coppolino, Lorenzo Pugliese, Anna Maria Sponta, Loreta Tobia, Elio Tolli, Pierfrancesco Zito, Valerio Bonavolontà, Leila Fabiani, Chiara Tuccella, Maria Giulia Vinciguerra, Giovanni Fiorilli, Andrea Buonsenso
pmc-12452330.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: Previous studies showed that workplace physical activity programs (WPAPs) could improve general health among employees. However, there is a lack of correlation between oxidative redox status and the metabolic and physical fitness (PF) of workers. The objective of the study was to evaluate the improvements of a 24-week combined circuit training and mobility training program on PF, oxidative redox status, and metabolic parameters on healthy academic employees.

pmc-12586905.title: Canopy Carbon‐ and Water‐Use Efficiencies in Response to Temperature and Water Deficit for Wheat
pmc-12586905.creator: Liang Fang, Paul C Struik, Xinyou Yin, Pierre Martre
pmc-12586905.description: The frequency and intensity of extreme climatic events increase the complexity in assessing climate change impacts on (agro)ecosystem functions and crop production. A better understanding of carbon and water fluxes for crop plants under climate change requires research based on direct canopy‐scale measurements.

pmc-13066840.title: Factors predicting the risk of breast cancer: construction and validation of a nomogram model
pmc-13066840.creator: Tong Ren, Rong Huang, Weijun Xiao, Xiaoping Huang, Jingting Yan, Qiao Ji, Yihua Song, Yanan Guo, Xiang Li, Mo Yang, Zuofeng Xu, Fengping Liang
pmc-13066840.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundA simple and practicable strategy for predicting the risk of breast cancer (BC) urgently needs to be established. This study aimed to construct a nomogram model based on age and ultrasound (US) features to predict BC.MethodsConsecutive adult females with a breast mass who underwent breast US followed by biopsy or surgery (Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS) categories III–V) or who received follow-up US more than 6 months after the initial US (BI-RADS category II) from August 2020 to November 2023

pmc-13216258.title: X-ray and γ-ray beam interstellar communication and implications for SETI
pmc-13216258.creator: Lucas Beveridge, Gerrit Bruhaug
pmc-13216258.description: The possibility of detecting artificial signals transmitted by alien civilizations via collimated X-ray or gamma-ray beams is investigated. The prospect of using such beams for human communication within the solar system and beyond is also discussed. Detector responses were simulated for input signals and analyzed using relative entropy. For simplicity, all signals were assumed to use on-off keying (OOK) modulation.

pmc-13264714.title: Atrial septal defect assessment: challenges of 4D cardiac computed tomography
pmc-13264714.creator: Aeos Gaea Baldevia, Douglas Corsi, Yasmin S. Hamirani
pmc-13264714.description: rly in minimally invasive robotic surgery, where precise patch selection and limited operative exposure demand reliable preoperative imaging (2). Although echocardiography remains the standard diagnostic modality, its assessment may be influenced by acoustic window limitations and operator dependency (2). In contrast, CT offers superior spatial resolution, and 4D CT enables phase-specific visualization of cardiac structures throughout the cardiac cycle.

pmc-13351313.title: Emerging Novel SARS‐CoV‐2 Subvariants and the Advantages of AI‐ML in Deciphering the Mutation Trends, Genomic Surveillance and Vaccine Development
pmc-13351313.creator: Aurobinda Rout, Kumarjit Das, Ashish K Sarangi, Snehasish Mishra, Chandana Mohanty, Puneet K Singh, Swikrutee Rout, Ranjan K Mohapatra, Lawrence Sena Tuglo
pmc-13351313.description: Background and AimThe world witnessed COVID‐19 in 2025 yet again, a resurgence driven by LF.7 and NB.1.8.1 subvariants of JN.1. With Singapore, Hong Kong and Thailand as the epicenter this time, these variants demonstrated rapid geographic spread and temporal dominance across regions including India, the United States (US), the United Kingdom (UK), and China.

pmc-13406349.creator: Tzayaka Castillo-Mendieta, Stephanie Sánchez-Torres, Hermelinda Salgado-Ceballos, Julia J. Segura-Uribe, Julio Morán, Christian Guerra-Araiza, Angélica Coyoy-Salgado

pmc-13585484.title: Use of EN Snare Device for Successful Retrieval of a Pigtail Catheter Straightener after Iliac Artery Stent Placement: A Case Report
pmc-13585484.creator: Takeshi Wada, Katsutoshi Takayama, Kaoru Myouchin
pmc-13585484.description: Percutaneous retrieval is a well-established, minimally invasive method for removing foreign bodies from blood vessels. We experienced a 77-year-old man in whom a radiolucent pigtail catheter straightener had been mis-inserted into the abdominal aorta and was successfully retrieved using an EN Snare device.

pmc-13679352.title: Beyond static frailty: longitudinal trajectories, nonlinear associations, and muscle strength mediation in osteoporosis risk
pmc-13679352.creator: Junyu Zhou, Jui-Hua Wang, Zhen Huang, Liping Cao
pmc-13679352.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundFrailty, a multidimensional indicator of declining physiological reserve, has been consistently linked to adverse health outcomes. However, whether dynamic trajectories of the Frailty Index (FI) predict new-onset osteoporosis remains unclear.MethodsFor this longitudinal cohort study, we retrieved data on adults aged ≥50 years from the Health and Retirement Study, the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing, and the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe.

pmc-13680301.title: Ontogenetic shifts in the metabolomic profiles of Battus polydamas (Lepidoptera: Papilionidae: Troidini) Feeding on Aristolochia gigantea
pmc-13680301.creator: Sofia Coradini Schirmer, Thomas Christopher Rhys Williams, Jefferson Brendon Almeida dos Reis
pmc-13680301.description: Insect development involves profound physiological reorganization that can alter the assimilation and allocation of metabolites across life stages. In herbivorous insects, these processes are tightly linked to diet-derived chemical exposure, yet how metabolic organization shifts throughout ontogeny remains poorly understood.

uslaw-usc-t43-s617e.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t43-s617e.description: United States Code, Title 43 (Public Lands); Chapter 12A (Boulder Canyon Project); Subchapter I (Boulder Canyon Project Act). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The dam and reservoir provided for by section 617 of this title shall be used: First, for river regulation, improvement of navigation, and flood control; second, for irrigation and domestic uses and satisfaction of present perfected rights in pursuance.
